chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya said:

I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who had a debt due from another man, so he gifted it to his son. The man mentioned the money that was due from him to the other, and he said to him: 'There is nothing upon you regarding it in this world and the hereafter, provided that pleases him, and he had indeed gifted it to a son of his.' He said: 'Yes, it is that he gifted it to him, then he revoked it and made it a gift to this one.'

key_terms.فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ: in this world and the hereafter

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on revoking a gift of a debt from one son to another?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal status of revoking a gift of debt (*hibah al-dayn*), ruling that if the original recipient accepts the revocation willingly, he is released from the obligation in both the worldly and spiritual realms. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic principle that the transfer of debt via gift is binding and can be reversed with mutual consent, distinguishing it from simple repayment. The emphasis on 'pleasing the recipient' (*yatiyyabu lihi*) highlights the importance of the donee's satisfaction in the validity of the revocation process.
